subtopics.title: Major Bases of the Demand
subtopics.summary: Supporters argue that the Darjeeling Hills population has a distinct linguistic, cultural and social identity compared with the Bengali-majority plains. Concerns over identity insecurity and racial stereotyping have strengthened demands for stronger political recognition and representation. Economic concerns cover infrastructure, employment, developmental neglect and insufficient political and fiscal autonomy.
facts: The Darjeeling Hills population has a distinct linguistic, cultural and social identity compared with the Bengali-majority plains
The region has a predominantly Nepali-speaking population
Identity insecurity and racial stereotyping have contributed to demands for stronger political recognition and representation
Proponents seek recognition of the community as an integral part of India, rather than separation from the country
Inadequate infrastructure is a long-standing economic concern
Limited employment opportunities and developmental neglect are raised as concerns
Insufficient political and fiscal autonomy is a concern
The region contributes through sectors such as Darjeeling Tea, Forestry and Tourism

subtopics.title: Current Process and Challenges
subtopics.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs recently convened a Tripartite Meeting with the Government of West Bengal and Gorkha community representatives. The Union Government then constituted a committee headed by Pankaj Kumar Singh to work out modalities for a Permanent Political Solution. The challenges include opposition to territorial division, the region's strategic location, fragmented Gorkha politics and economic sustainability.
facts: The Ministry of Home Affairs recently convened a Tripartite Meeting with the Government of West Bengal and Gorkha community representatives
The Union Government constituted a committee headed by Pankaj Kumar Singh
The committee will examine the issue within the Constitutional Framework, including governance, financial assistance and development support
The committee will also work out a roadmap for granting Scheduled Tribe status to 11 Gorkha communities
Opposition in parts of West Bengal to territorial division reflects concerns over territorial integrity and administrative cohesion
The Darjeeling region occupies the Siliguri Corridor (Chicken's Neck), close to Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh
The Siliguri Corridor is the principal land link between mainland India and the Northeast
Prolonged instability in the region can have wider strategic and national security implications
Gorkha Janmukti Morcha and Gorkha National Liberation Front are among several groups, making a common position difficult
The regional economy depends on tea, tourism and related activities, which face structural and seasonal challenges
